history.note: Row removed: Cohere does not bill Rerank per token, so $0.02 per 1M tokens is a figure in a unit the vendor has no rate for — no re-capture could ever corroborate it. Cohere's own pricing documentation states "Our Rerank models are priced based on the quantity of searches, and our Embedding models are priced based on the number of tokens embedded", and a search unit is 1 query x up to 100 documents, so there is no fixed token count to convert through either. Read live 2026-09-14 with all four cohere.com/pricing tabs clicked (52,856 chars, three clicks landed): the pay-as-you-go "Advanced retrieval models" card lists Embed 4 ($0.12 / 1M tokens), Rerank 4 Fast ($2.00 / 1K searches) and Rerank 4 Pro ($2.50 / 1K searches) — Rerank 3.5 is not on it, and the string "0.02" does not appear anywhere in the four-tab render. Rerank 3.5 survives on that page in exactly one place, the Model Vault committed-instance table (Medium, $5.00/hr, $3,250/mo), which is not a per-token rate. The model is still live (rerank-v3.5 is listed on docs.cohere.com/docs/models and is not in Cohere's deprecations), so this is NOT a retirement: a Retired row would tell readers the model is no longer served, which is false. Our schema cannot express "no price" — validate_dataset requires input_per_mtok to be a number and price_unit carries per_token only — so the choice was to publish a number Cohere does not charge or to omit the row. Charter: omit a model rather than publish a wrong price for it. CEO ruling on MOD-729, 2026-09-14. Receipts kept at data/evidence/cohere-rerank-3-5/.
history.public_note: Removed because Cohere does not sell Rerank 3.5 by the token. Cohere bills reranking per search — its current card prices Rerank 4 Fast at $2.00 and Rerank 4 Pro at $2.50 per 1,000 searches — and publishes no per-token rate for any Rerank model, so the $0.02 per 1M tokens we carried was never a Cohere price. Rerank 3.5 itself is still available; only its per-token figure was unsourceable, and we would rather show you nothing than a number nobody charges. Cohere lists Rerank 3.5 only under committed instances ($5.00/hr, $3,250/mo).

history.note: A 2026-06-25 scrape wrote an unsourced output_per_mtok=$1.00 placeholder into all 7 tracked Groq models at once and held it across six snapshots until a verified scrape reverted it on 2026-07-04. The identical $1.00 across a whole provider, with no `source` field, is a scrape/parse fallback, not a market move (it manufactured 12 phantom price moves incl. a +707.7% on Llama 3.1 8B Instant). The true output price was unchanged across the span (verified equal on both sides of the gap). Data correction: the phantom span is flattened to the true value; this boundary point is relabeled from a price-move event to `correction` and supersedes the placeholder span.

history.note: Row removed: Granite 4 H Large is not a product. IBM's watsonx.ai rate card enumerates every Granite SKU including the ones it does not sell per token (granite-4h-micro and granite-4h-tiny both print "Not available" on the same table that prices granite-4h-small at USD 0.0636/0.265) — and there is no medium or large row on it, read live 2026-08-14. OpenRouter routes no endpoint; the row is absent from litellm_id_map, so nothing has ever watched this price. Granite 4.0 Large was never announced, let alone released. The published $0.30/$1.20 is a v2.0 bulk-seed tier default, shared byte-for-byte with 11 other rows, not an observation. No seller exists, so publishing any price for it is fabrication.

history.note: Published $0.06/$0.25 was never IBM's printed price: it traces to a 2025-10-20 litellm-archive backfill (confidence: reconstructed) and was never read off IBM. IBM's watsonx.ai rate card — this row's own pricing_url, and its own committed 2026-08-09 receipt — prints granite-4h-small at USD 0.0636 per 1M tokens input / USD 0.265 output, and printed the same on us-en on 2026-08-14. The 6% gap is IBM's own uniform uplift over round base rates, applied across the whole table (granite-8b-code-instruct USD 0.636, granite-guardian-3-8b USD 0.212, llama-3-3-70b USD 0.7526, mistral-small-3-1 USD 0.106/0.318) — not tax (the footnote excludes taxes and duties) and not country variance (us-en is identical). The sibling row ibm-granite-embedding-278m already publishes the uplifted USD 0.106 off this same table. IBM did not re-price: this is our number being corrected to the rate card, not a market move.

history.note: Published $0.10/$0.10 was never a Mistral price: it entered at the 2026-06-25 hand baseline and carried forward for 78 days. Mistral's own pricing page lists Pixtral 12B (api endpoint pixtral-12b) at $0.15 in / $0.15 out under Open models in every archived capture read from 2025-05-25 through 2025-12-31 - the last capture before the SKU was retired from the Mistral API on 2025-12-31 still prints $0.15/$0.15, so $0.15/$0.15 is the archival last first-party rate. Corroborated three ways: LiteLLM's DATED mistral/pixtral-12b-2409 entry carries $0.15/$0.15 with deprecation_date 2025-12-31 == our retired_on; the Vercel AI Gateway pass-through (vercel_ai_gateway/mistral/pixtral-12b) carries $0.15/$0.15; and this row's own litellm-archive backfill points (2024-10-03 and 2026-06-23) both read $0.15/$0.15, i.e. the reference catalog never carried $0.10 either. Positive control on the same captures: the sibling Pixtral Large row reads $2/$6, exactly what we already publish. Data correction, not a market move - Mistral did not raise this price on 2026-09-11; the SKU has been retired since 2025-12-31. Supersedes the wrong baseline and carried-forward span.
